name: Pseudo-perplexity agreement between reference and efficient implementations (Saadat and Fellay 2026 Figure 1)
description: Per-sequence pseudo-perplexity from the reference implementation and the efficient implementation on 50 synthetic 1000-length sequences, compared by Pearson correlation.

attributes.protocol: Compute masked-LM pseudo-perplexity (one position masked at a time, padding and special tokens excluded) for each of 50 uniform random sequences of length 1000 with the reference and the efficient implementation; report the Pearson correlation across sequences.
attributes.metric_definition: Pearson r between per-sequence pseudo-perplexity of the reference and the efficient implementation (Appendix A.2, Eq. 2)
attributes.version: ICLR 2026 workshop paper, Section 3.1 and Appendix A.2
limitations: Synthetic sequences at one length; the authors note it does not cover longer contexts or real genomic sequence.
r is printed to two decimals inside the figure; per-sequence values are plotted, not printed.
Numeric precision of each run (BF16 or FP32) is not stated.

Figure 1 axes (labelled 'Perplexity') run from about 15,000 to 30,000 for the NT models, above the size of the NT 6-mer vocabulary (about 4,100 tokens; Dalla-Torre et al., not stated in this paper), so the NT models score uniform random DNA worse than a uniform guess. The paper does not comment on this.

Section 2.3 says attention stays exact when quantization is off, yet NT 2.5B prints r = 0.98 with visibly scattered points. The paper does not explain the difference; numeric precision may contribute.
attributes.source_locator: Section 2.4 'Evaluation axes and metrics' item 1 and 'Data'; Section 3.1; Figure 1 (page 4); Appendix A.2

description: Peak GPU memory of a training step at sequence length 1000 and batch size 16, adding FlashAttention, activation checkpointing and ZeRO Stage-2 CPU offload in turn.

attributes.protocol: Measure peak allocated GPU memory (PyTorch allocator statistics) during training at sequence length 1000 and batch size 16, for the baseline and after cumulatively adding FlashAttention, activation checkpointing and ZeRO Stage-2 CPU offload (DeepSpeed), on an NVIDIA H100.
attributes.memory_measurement: Peak allocated GPU memory from the framework allocator statistics during the measured region (Appendix A.3)
limitations: Only the stage values quoted in Section 3.3 are printed; the other Figure 3 points are plotted without values.

The training input is not named. The paper lists synthetic sequences as its input for implementation measurements and the promoter and enhancer tasks as its only real data; the training ablation is linked to the synthetic data on that basis.

Whether the ablation trains with LoRA (the stated default for fine-tuning) or updates all weights is not stated. Section 3.3 attributes the NT 2.5B ZeRO saving to optimizer state dominating, which fits a full-weight update better than LoRA rank 16 on query, key and value projections, but the paper does not say.
Whether 'sequence length 1000' counts nucleotides or tokens is not stated; NT uses 6-mer tokens and GENA-LM uses BPE tokens, so the two families see different token counts for 1000 nucleotides.
Single hardware type (H100 94GB); offload benefit depends on CPU-GPU bandwidth, as the authors note.

attributes.source_discrepancy: Section 2.4 says the quantization experiment measures parameter memory, and Section 3.5 opens 'Quantization reduces parameter memory' before giving these values, but the Figure 5 right panel is labelled 'Peak Memory (GB)'. A 1.1 GB drop is small for parameters alone (2.5 billion weights are about 5 GB in BF16 and about 1.25 GB at 4 bits; an extractor's estimate, not printed), so the values look like peak memory of a run whose input length, batch size and quantised layers ('a conservative strategy for NT models') are not stated. Recorded as peak memory. Independent review 2026-10-15: the Figure 5 right-panel bars for NT 2.5B also do not match the printed sentence. Against the panel's gridlines they stand at about 6.6 GB (BF16) and about 5.45 GB (4-bit), against 6.7 and 5.6 in the text (reviewer's reading of bar heights, not a printed value). The direction and size of the drop agree, so the printed values are kept with this note and no source-level concern is raised.
